clue.text: Boorish American is historically a rich Republican leader

parts.note: boorish means crass, coarse and insensitive

explanation.surface: A crude American is described as a wealthy party boss of the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' points at US politics, but the republic is Rome's: Crassus was a general and the richest man of the late Roman Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Licinius Crassus, ally of Caesar and Pompey, was famed as the wealthiest leader of the Roman Republic.

clue.text: Transport rich ass in time to see Colosseum unfortunates

indicators.note: transport means carry off or move, so the letters are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving a wealthy donkey in good time to watch the doomed victims in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Early Christians were famously thrown to lions as spectacle, the arena's unfortunate victims in Rome.

clue.text: Defences of troops are ultimately submerged by rising Tyrrhenian?

indicators.note: submerged by means the troops and the final letter are swallowed beneath the rising water
rising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Tyrrhenian is a sea off western Italy; the query marks it as one example
GIs are American soldiers, troops

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of are

explanation.surface: Coastal troop defences are eventually swamped as the Tyrrhenian rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyrrhenian is a sea west of Italy; the query flags it as just one example of a sea, and 'rising' turns that word upward in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An aegis was the shield of Zeus or Athena, so the plural means protections or shields.

clue.text: Rock shelter almost completed

indicators.note: almost completed means the word stops just short of its last letter

parts.note: a screen gives shelter or cover

explanation.surface: A shelter carved from rock is nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the mass of loose broken rock on a mountain slope.

clue.text: Fleet sails west into foreign territories taking their capitals

indicators.note: taking their capitals means using the initial letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A navy sails westward into foreign lands, seizing their capital cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' reads as a navy, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means fast or nimble, as in fleet of foot.

clue.text: Tread in Tiber having being drained enough

indicators.note: a word drained of its contents keeps only its shell, here the first and last letters of Tiber

parts.note: ample means enough, sufficient

explanation.surface: Wading into the Tiber is easy enough now that the river has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something, crushing it underfoot.

clue.text: No interlude perhaps during vulgar social event

indicators.note: during means these letters fall inside the vulgar word

parts.note: tarty means cheaply showy or vulgar
O is nought, the figure for no
a gap, such as an interlude, is a break or interval

explanation.surface: No break in the middle of some crude party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party where the guests wear bedsheets as Roman togas is a kind of social gathering.

clue.text: 9 Across and son needing joint command on galley, say

parts.note: the answer to 9 Across means concerning, which is about
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A son needs a shared order for a ship, cross-referenced to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailing order to go about, turning the vessel onto the other tack, is shouted on board ships like galleys.

clue.text: Write piece about oneself being an emperor?

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: about means the gun goes around the letter for oneself

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun
I is the word for oneself, the speaker

explanation.surface: Composing an autobiographical piece about being an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'emperor' is an example: the emperor penguin.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is the largest species of this flightless Antarctic bird.

clue.text: Vessel in underground channel has section removed

indicators.note: removed says the letter for section is taken out of the channel

parts.note: a sewer is an underground channel for waste

explanation.surface: A boat in a drain has part of it cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Seeing dagger in Caesar's back twisted

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of Caesar
twisted says the letters of dagger, in and the final R are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone looks on as a dagger is driven, twisting, into Caesar's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caesar's back' gives R, the last letter of Caesar; 'twisted' then shuffles DAGGER, IN and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing and the other word both mean 'considering' or 'concerning', as in 'seeing that' a fact applies.

clue.text: Old relative forgetting Latin for 'cat'

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so the letter for Latin drops out of the relative

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: An elderly relative cannot recall the Latin word for 'cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat of the Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Dubious cult infiltrated by The Independent quietly

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the cult has other letters slipped inside it

parts.note: a sect is a cult or breakaway religious group
the newspaper setting the puzzle speaks of itself as us
P (piano) is the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A shady cult has been infiltrated by an undercover reporter from this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is the paper this puzzle appears in, so it is 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is doubtful or questionable, just as a dubious claim invites mistrust.

clue.text: Finds shelter for youth stabbed by nameless maniacs

indicators.note: stabbed by means the youth is pierced, with other letters thrust into him

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky young man, a youth

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation N for name is taken away

parts.note: nuts are maniacs, crazy people

explanation.surface: A young man is knifed by a gang of anonymous lunatics.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up is the phrasal verb for giving them a bed or lodging for a while.

clue.text: Servant crosses overthrown city nearly speechless delivering note

indicators.note: crosses means the servant straddles the city's letters

parts.note: a man is a manservant

indicators.note: overthrown means turned upside down, so the city is reversed

parts.note: Rome is the city of the series theme

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: dumb means speechless

explanation.surface: A slave, struck dumb by the fall of the city, carries a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a written note or memo recording something.

clue.text: It could be stuck between pages of fashionable collection

definitions.text: It could be stuck between pages

parts.note: in means fashionable, in vogue
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: Something tucked into a stylish album or catalogue between its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is an extra sheet or leaflet slipped inside a magazine or book.

clue.text: Mid-range hospital in forest could be found by seaman

indicators.note: in places the hospital letter within the forest

parts.note: a forest is many trees
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A medium-sized hospital in woodland, discovered by a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel or restaurant rated with three stars sits in the middle of the quality scale.

clue.text: Maybe fish spear lacks tip

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: lacks tip means the first letter of the weapon is missing

parts.note: a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: Perhaps a fishing spear has lost its point.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is an old-fashioned synonym for perhaps or possibly.

clue.text: Made progress organising sprees with family leader

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters of sprees are put in a new order

parts.note: a don is the head of a Mafia family

explanation.surface: A crime boss got ahead by arranging wild parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to carry on determinedly, so pressing on is making progress.

clue.text: Pity Nero. To lose power when rebuilding reputation

indicators.note: to lose something is to give it up, so the letter for power is dropped from the pool
rebuilding says the remaining letters are put together again in a new order

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Pity poor Nero, who lost power while rebuilding Rome after the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P out of PITYNEROTO and rearrange the other nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame of a bad kind, an unflattering reputation.

clue.text: Delay broadcast about criminal

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the broadcast word is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast
a lag, as in old lag, is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A transmission held back because it concerns a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delay broadcast' looks like a single instruction, but 'Delay' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is an interval or hold-up between one event and another.

clue.text: Philosopher has a change of heart … there is a god

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letter of the philosopher is swapped for another, A becoming U

parts.note: Plato was the Athenian philosopher, pupil of Socrates

explanation.surface: A thinker has a sudden conversion and declares that God exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was the Roman god of the underworld, counterpart of the Greek Hades.

clue.text: Person who announces absolute ruler

parts.note: utter means absolute, complete
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A herald proclaims a tyrant with total power.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to say it aloud, so one who utters speaks or declares.

clue.text: Wicked types hampering the Spanish forces

indicators.note: hampering means the wicked types surround and hold up the Spanish word

parts.note: imps are mischievous little devils, wicked types
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Villains are obstructing the Spanish armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forces' looks like a noun for troops, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone into acting, so it forces them on.

clue.text: Picks woven carpet to cover interior of villa

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged carpet goes over and around the other letter
woven suggests threads interlaced, so the letters of carpet are rearranged
the interior of a word is its central letter, here the middle of villa

explanation.surface: A rug made to lie over the floor inside a Roman villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectra (plural of plectrum) are the small picks used to pluck guitar or lute strings.

clue.text: Suggest flower of Italy's the best

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river, a flower in the sense of something that flows; the possessive adds S
it means the very best, the ultimate thing

explanation.surface: Proposing that some Italian bloom is the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword pun: something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea for consideration.

clue.text: Climbing part of tree-lined Aventine to make escape

indicators.note: Climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Scaling part of Rome's leafy Aventine Hill in order to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aventine is one of the seven hills of Rome; 'Climbing' turns the hidden letters upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or slip away from someone or something.

clue.text: Greeting arrival from the heavens

definitions.meaning: a salute or welcome called out to someone
frozen pellets of rain falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A welcome arriving from above.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a call of welcome; the other is icy precipitation dropping from clouds.

clue.text: Distribute a fair amount according to reports

indicators.note: according to reports means what we hear, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a lot is a fair amount, plenty

explanation.surface: Sharing out a reasonable quantity, as the reports say.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or apportion portions among people.

clue.text: Lost hope after pater consumed by wish to join daughter

indicators.note: to join means the daughter is attached on the end
consumed by means the father is swallowed inside the wish

parts.note: a desire is a wish
pater is old public-school slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: A father, swallowed up by the longing to be reunited with his daughter, gave up hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who despaired gave up all expectation that things would improve.

clue.text: Shackle soldiers traversing river

indicators.note: traversing means the soldiers stretch across, with the river inside them

parts.note: a legion is a body of Roman soldiers
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A legion crossing a river in chains.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg iron is a metal shackle fastened round a prisoner's ankle.

clue.text: Proposition of article has Rome shocked

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: shocked suggests being shaken up, so the letters of Rome are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A newspaper article's suggestion has scandalised Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical proposition that has been or can be proved.
